IMPORT `rbo-domain`
IMPORT `rbo-part2-retail-barring-orders`
IMPORT `rbo-part3-varying-or-cancelling`
IMPORT `rbo-part5-service-and-firearms`

-- Retail Barring Orders Bill 2025 (WA) -- worked cases and assertions.
--
-- The assertions marked INCIDENT are the ones that carry a finding in
-- INCIDENTS.md. PIPELINE.md's standard is that "every finding is traceable to a
-- provision and reproducible by machine": an incident that cannot be
-- demonstrated by an assertion or a worked scenario is an opinion, not a
-- finding. These are the demonstrations.
--
-- BUILDING A DATE. There is no date literal and no date constructor in scope,
-- because `daydate` is not installed (H-04). `TODATE` is a compiler builtin and
-- returns `MAYBE DATE`, so every fixture that needs a date takes it as a GIVEN
-- and the assertion site unwraps the MAYBE. The NOTHING arms are unreachable
-- for the literal strings used here -- `TODATE "2026-03-01"` cannot fail -- and
-- they return FALSE rather than refusing, so an arm that somehow WERE reached
-- would fail its assertion loudly instead of passing quietly. `REFUSE` is not
-- available in this build either, which is why FALSE is the fallback.

§ `Worked cases`

§§ `Parties and places`

`Northbridge IGA` MEANS Premises WITH
    `name`                                 IS "Northbridge IGA"
    `a retail business is conducted on it` IS TRUE
    `part of a retail shopping centre`     IS FALSE

`Dale` MEANS Person WITH
    `name` IS "Dale"
    `age`  IS `an adult`

§§ `A firearms RBO`

-- s 15(3)(f) restraint present, so this is a `firearms RBO` within s 63(1).
GIVEN `the day it came into force` IS A DATE
GIVETH AN RBO
`the firearms RBO against Dale in force from` `the day it came into force` MEANS RBO WITH
    `person who is bound`                    IS `Dale`
    `age when the RBO was made`              IS `an adult`
    `premises stated in the application`      IS `Northbridge IGA`
    `period specified in days`                IS NOTHING
    `came into force on`                      IS `the day it came into force`
    `prohibits possession of a firearm item`  IS TRUE

-- Dale uses a firearm at work: a security contractor whose employer holds the
-- authorisation. This is squarely the case s 63(4) is for.
`Dale uses a firearm at work` MEANS FirearmsCircumstances WITH
    `the restrained person uses a firearm item in their usual occupation` IS TRUE
    `a co-licensee holds an authorisation for the same firearm item`      IS FALSE

§ `B-01 -- section 39(2) has no power to dismiss`

-- The two enumerations, read straight off s 39(1) and s 39(2).
#EVAL `the orders the court may make under section 39` `section 37 -- an inter partes hearing`
#EVAL `the orders the court may make under section 39` `section 38(1)(a) -- a cancellation heard in the absence of the person bound`

-- INCIDENT B-01. At a s 37 hearing the court may dismiss; at a s 38(1)(a)
-- hearing it may not. The pair is the finding: the power exists in the Bill,
-- and the subsection that most needs it does not confer it.
#ASSERT `the court may dismiss the application at this hearing` `section 37 -- an inter partes hearing`
#ASSERT NOT (`the court may dismiss the application at this hearing` `section 38(1)(a) -- a cancellation heard in the absence of the person bound`)

-- INCIDENT B-01, the consequence. A cancellation application that the court
-- declines to grant is left with no order by which it can be disposed of.
#ASSERT (`the outcome under section 39` `section 38(1)(a) -- a cancellation heard in the absence of the person bound` FALSE) EQUALS `no order is available under section 39`

-- The control. The same facts at a s 37 hearing resolve, which is what shows
-- the gap belongs to s 39(2) and not to the fact pattern.
#ASSERT (`the outcome under section 39` `section 37 -- an inter partes hearing` FALSE) EQUALS `the application is dismissed`

-- And the court that IS satisfied can cancel at either hearing, so nothing
-- above is an artefact of the cancellation power being missing.
#ASSERT (`the outcome under section 39` `section 38(1)(a) -- a cancellation heard in the absence of the person bound` TRUE) EQUALS `the RBO is cancelled`
#ASSERT (`the outcome under section 39` `section 37 -- an inter partes hearing` TRUE) EQUALS `the RBO is cancelled`

§ `B-02 -- the firearms notification chain breaks on six of nine service routes`

-- Every route in the Bill is good service. Stated first, because the finding is
-- that service and the firearms inquiry come apart, and that requires both
-- halves on the record.
#ASSERT `the relevant order is served` `personal service by a prison officer`
#ASSERT `the relevant order is served` `substituted service effected by post`
#ASSERT `the relevant order is served` `service taken to have been effected by presence in court`
#ASSERT `the relevant order is served` `personal service by a police officer`

-- The s 63(2) duty, route by route. Two routes carry it.
#ASSERT `section 63(2) obliges the server to ask the firearms questions` `personal service by a police officer`
#ASSERT `section 63(2) obliges the server to ask the firearms questions` `substituted service effected orally by a police officer`

-- And seven do not.
#ASSERT NOT (`section 63(2) obliges the server to ask the firearms questions` `personal service by a registrar of the court`)
#ASSERT NOT (`section 63(2) obliges the server to ask the firearms questions` `personal service by a person authorised by a registrar`)
#ASSERT NOT (`section 63(2) obliges the server to ask the firearms questions` `personal service by a custodial officer`)
#ASSERT NOT (`section 63(2) obliges the server to ask the firearms questions` `personal service by a prison officer`)
#ASSERT NOT (`section 63(2) obliges the server to ask the firearms questions` `service taken to have been effected by presence in court`)
#ASSERT NOT (`section 63(2) obliges the server to ask the firearms questions` `substituted service effected by post`)
#ASSERT NOT (`section 63(2) obliges the server to ask the firearms questions` `substituted service effected by electronic means`)

-- INCIDENT B-02, scenario A: personal service by a prison officer. Good
-- service, firearms RBO, Dale uses a firearm at work -- and the Commissioner's
-- s 63(4) duty never arises, so the s 63(5) offence cannot be committed by the
-- employer who holds the authorisation.
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`B-02 scenario A -- prison officer serves personally` MEANS
    CONSIDER TODATE "2026-03-01"
    WHEN NOTHING THEN FALSE
    WHEN JUST `the day` THEN
            `the relevant order is served` `personal service by a prison officer`
        AND NOT (`the Commissioner must notify under section 63(4)` (`the firearms RBO against Dale in force from` `the day`) `personal service by a prison officer` `Dale uses a firearm at work`)
        AND NOT (`a responsible person could commit the section 63(5) offence` (`the firearms RBO against Dale in force from` `the day`) `personal service by a prison officer` `Dale uses a firearm at work`)

#ASSERT `B-02 scenario A -- prison officer serves personally`

-- INCIDENT B-02, scenario B: substituted service by post, approved by a senior
-- police officer under s 57(1) and effected by a police officer. Still no duty,
-- because s 63(2) reaches substituted service only where effected ORALLY.
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`B-02 scenario B -- substituted service by post` MEANS
    CONSIDER TODATE "2026-03-01"
    WHEN NOTHING THEN FALSE
    WHEN JUST `the day` THEN
            `the relevant order is served` `substituted service effected by post`
        AND NOT (`the Commissioner must notify under section 63(4)` (`the firearms RBO against Dale in force from` `the day`) `substituted service effected by post` `Dale uses a firearm at work`)

#ASSERT `B-02 scenario B -- substituted service by post`

-- INCIDENT B-02, scenario C: the person is in court when the order is made, so
-- s 54(2) deems personal service with no server at all. This is the commonest
-- case and the one where the person is most easily questioned.
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`B-02 scenario C -- deemed service by presence in court` MEANS
    CONSIDER TODATE "2026-03-01"
    WHEN NOTHING THEN FALSE
    WHEN JUST `the day` THEN
            `the relevant order is served` `service taken to have been effected by presence in court`
        AND NOT (`the Commissioner must notify under section 63(4)` (`the firearms RBO against Dale in force from` `the day`) `service taken to have been effected by presence in court` `Dale uses a firearm at work`)

#ASSERT `B-02 scenario C -- deemed service by presence in court`

-- The control. Change ONLY the service route to the one s 63(2) names, on
-- identical facts, and the whole chain fires. This is what makes the three
-- scenarios above findings about s 63(2) rather than about the fixture.
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
`B-02 control -- a police officer serves personally` MEANS
    CONSIDER TODATE "2026-03-01"
    WHEN NOTHING THEN FALSE
    WHEN JUST `the day` THEN
            `the Commissioner must notify under section 63(4)` (`the firearms RBO against Dale in force from` `the day`) `personal service by a police officer` `Dale uses a firearm at work`
        AND `a responsible person could commit the section 63(5) offence` (`the firearms RBO against Dale in force from` `the day`) `personal service by a police officer` `Dale uses a firearm at work`

#ASSERT `B-02 control -- a police officer serves personally`

§ `Sanity -- section 21 duration`

`an RBO on Dale with no period specified` MEANS
    CONSIDER TODATE "2026-03-01"
    WHEN NOTHING THEN 0
    WHEN JUST `the day` THEN
        `the period for which the RBO remains in force, in days` (`the firearms RBO against Dale in force from` `the day`)

-- s 21(3)(b): no period specified, adult -- 2 years.
#ASSERT `an RBO on Dale with no period specified` EQUALS 730

-- s 21(2): the ceiling the court may specify, for each age class.
#ASSERT (`the maximum period in days` `an adult`) EQUALS 730
#ASSERT (`the maximum period in days` `a child`) EQUALS 365

-- Retail Barring Orders Bill 2025 (WA), Bill No. 47 -- shared ontology.
--
-- This module carries the types the operative modules share. It states no rule:
-- every `DECLARE` here is a fact-shape, and every predicate over it lives in the
-- module for the Part that enacts it.
--
-- Source: sources/bill-47-1.txt, extracted with `pdftotext -layout` from
-- Bill+47-1.002.pdf (sha256 bc504a511cac03e97cc462a5eb3ca1578f493e726b6f072bf
-- a89887602f9fb73). Section and line references throughout are to that extract.
--
-- NO IMPORTS. The `l4` on this machine ships without its standard library
-- (incident H-04) and an unresolvable IMPORT typechecks clean (H-03), so an
-- `IMPORT prelude` line here would be a claim this file cannot cash. Everything
-- below uses compiler builtins only -- records, enums, CONSIDER, LIST, and the
-- DATE_DAY/DATE_MONTH/DATE_YEAR accessors.
--
-- HOUSE STYLE. Inert style: the statutory words ride as inert strings in the
-- scaffolding, and the operative atoms are short names the ladder can print and
-- the wizard can ask. Field names start at the complement, because the Saxon
-- genitive already supplies "is" and "has" -- `claim's `on retail premises``
-- reads "the claim IS on retail premises", so writing `is on retail premises`
-- says it twice.

§ `Part 1 -- Preliminary`

§§ `5 -- Terms used`

-- s 5: `adult` means a person who has reached 18 years of age; `child` means a
-- person under 18 years of age. The Bill uses the pair as a partition, and
-- every age-sensitive rule in it (ss 21(2), 28(2), 29(1), 33, 34(1), 40(2),
-- 48) branches on exactly one of the two. So it is ONE type with two
-- alternatives, not two booleans -- entry 6.3 of the phrasebook.
DECLARE Age IS ONE OF
    `an adult`
    `a child`

-- s 5: `premises` means the whole or any part of a building, place, stall,
-- structure, tent, vehicle or yard. Carried as an identity, because nothing in
-- the encoded slice turns on WHICH kind of structure it is -- only on whether
-- two references are to the same premises (entry 6.6: identity is a field you
-- compare, never the whole record).
DECLARE Premises HAS
    `name`                                   IS A STRING
    `a retail business is conducted on it`   IS A BOOLEAN
    `part of a retail shopping centre`       IS A BOOLEAN

-- s 5: `person who is bound`, in relation to an RBO, means the person named in
-- the RBO on whose lawful activities and behaviour restraints are imposed.
DECLARE Person HAS
    `name`          IS A STRING
    `age`           IS AN Age

§§ `6 -- Retail violence`

-- s 6(1)(a)-(e). Five limbs, kept as five independent booleans rather than an
-- enum: the subsection reads "engages in ANY of the following behaviour", so a
-- single incident may answer to several limbs at once, and a radio button would
-- lose that. Checkbox-relation pattern.
DECLARE Behaviour HAS
    `physical violence or abuse`                    IS A BOOLEAN   -- (a)
    `sexual violence or abuse`                      IS A BOOLEAN   -- (b)
    `threatening behaviour`                         IS A BOOLEAN   -- (c)
    `stalking`                                      IS A BOOLEAN   -- (d)
    `harassing, intimidating or offensive behaviour` IS A BOOLEAN  -- (e)

-- The fact pattern s 6(1) tests. Both the actor and the other person must be on
-- the retail premises: "if the person, WHILE ON retail premises, engages in ...
-- in relation to another person ON THE RETAIL PREMISES".
DECLARE Incident HAS
    `actor`                          IS A Person
    `premises`                       IS A Premises
    `the actor is on the premises`   IS A BOOLEAN
    `another person is on the premises` IS A BOOLEAN
    `behaviour`                      IS A Behaviour
    `date`                           IS A DATE
    -- s 6(2): a person who procures another to commit retail violence is taken
    -- to have also committed it. A deeming provision, so it is a fact about the
    -- incident and not a sixth limb of `Behaviour`.
    `the actor procured another to commit it` IS A BOOLEAN

§ `Part 2 -- Retail barring orders`

-- s 5: `retail barring order (RBO)` means an order made under section 10
-- imposing restraints of the kind referred to in section 15.
--
-- `period specified` is MAYBE by design and must not be folded into a total
-- enum: s 21(1) says the court MAY specify a period, and s 21(3) gives three
-- different default rules depending on whether one was specified and on the
-- person's age. The absence is a fact about the order, not a named outcome --
-- bucket 3 of drafting-patterns.md.
DECLARE RBO HAS
    `person who is bound`          IS A Person
    `age when the RBO was made`    IS AN Age
    `premises stated in the application` IS A Premises
    `period specified in days`     IS A MAYBE NUMBER
    `came into force on`           IS A DATE
    -- s 63(1): a `firearms RBO` is an RBO that prohibits a restrained person
    -- from being in possession of a firearm item. s 15(3)(f) is the restraint
    -- that makes it one.
    `prohibits possession of a firearm item` IS A BOOLEAN

§ `Part 5 -- General`

§§ `52 -- Term used: relevant order`

-- s 52: `relevant order` means (a) an RBO; or (b) an order under section
-- 39(1)(b) varying an RBO.
DECLARE RelevantOrder IS ONE OF
    `an RBO`
    `an order under section 39(1)(b) varying an RBO`

§§ `55, 57 -- How a relevant order is served`

-- s 55(2): personal service must be effected by one of five classes of person.
-- s 54(2): where the person bound is present in court when the order is made,
-- the order is TAKEN to have been served personally when it is made -- so there
-- is a sixth way for an order to become served, with no server at all.
-- s 57(6): substituted service may be prescribed orally, by post, or by email,
-- text message or other electronic means.
--
-- These are collapsed into one type because s 63(2) discriminates across all of
-- them at once: it asks both WHO served and HOW.
DECLARE ServiceRoute IS ONE OF
    `personal service by a registrar of the court`            -- s 55(2)(a)
    `personal service by a person authorised by a registrar`  -- s 55(2)(b)
    `personal service by a police officer`                    -- s 55(2)(c)
    `personal service by a custodial officer`                 -- s 55(2)(d)
    `personal service by a prison officer`                    -- s 55(2)(e)
    `service taken to have been effected by presence in court` -- s 54(2)
    `substituted service effected orally by a police officer`  -- s 57(6)(a)
    `substituted service effected by post`                     -- s 57(6)(b)
    `substituted service effected by electronic means`         -- s 57(6)(c)

§ `Part 3 -- Varying or cancelling an RBO`

-- s 39(1) and (2) enumerate what a court MAY order, and they enumerate
-- DIFFERENT sets depending on which section fixed the hearing. The disjunction
-- is the whole subject of incident B-01, so the orders are a type of their own
-- and the two subsections are two decisions returning lists over it.
DECLARE AvailableOrder IS ONE OF
    `dismissing the application to vary or cancel the RBO`   -- s 39(1)(a)
    `varying the RBO`                                        -- s 39(1)(b)
    `cancelling the RBO`                                     -- s 39(1)(c), (2)

-- Which section fixed the hearing. s 36 is the leave hearing on an application
-- by the person bound; s 37 is the ordinary inter partes hearing; s 38(1)(a) is
-- the hearing of a cancellation application that the applicant for the RBO has
-- asked, under s 34(3), to have heard in the absence of the person bound.
DECLARE HearingFixedUnder IS ONE OF
    `section 36(1)(a) -- a leave hearing`
    `section 37 -- an inter partes hearing`
    `section 38(1)(a) -- a cancellation heard in the absence of the person bound`

§§ `Dates`

-- NOT house style, and recorded as such. drafting-patterns.md builds date
-- windows with `daydate` -- `Day`, `Date`, leap-safe year increments. That
-- library is not installed here (H-04), so the comparison is done on the
-- components the compiler supplies directly. Rewrite this against `daydate`
-- once the library is available; the ONLY reason it is here is the missing
-- library, and nothing about the Bill called for it.
--
-- Lexicographic on (year, month, day). A BRANCH rather than a nested IF/ELSE
-- staircase: the arms are flat and first-match, which is what BRANCH says.
GIVEN `the earlier date` IS A DATE
      `the later date`   IS A DATE
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
DECIDE `the earlier date` `is on or before` `the later date` IF
    BRANCH
       IF DATE_YEAR  `the earlier date` LESS THAN    DATE_YEAR  `the later date` THEN TRUE
       IF DATE_YEAR  `the earlier date` GREATER THAN DATE_YEAR  `the later date` THEN FALSE
       IF DATE_MONTH `the earlier date` LESS THAN    DATE_MONTH `the later date` THEN TRUE
       IF DATE_MONTH `the earlier date` GREATER THAN DATE_MONTH `the later date` THEN FALSE
       OTHERWISE DATE_DAY `the earlier date` AT MOST DATE_DAY `the later date`

-- s 8(2)'s window. Written as a comparison against the incident date's
-- components with the YEAR incremented, rather than by constructing the
-- endpoint date, because constructing a DATE needs `daydate`'s YMD or Date and
-- no library is installed (H-04).
--
-- The leap edge, worked rather than assumed: an incident on 29 February 2024
-- gives a virtual bound of (2025, 2, 29), a day that does not exist. No real
-- application date can equal it, and the last real date at or before it is
-- 28 February 2025 -- which is also what `daydate`'s clamping `add months`
-- would yield. So the two agree on every input that can actually occur.
GIVEN `the application date` IS A DATE
      `the incident date`    IS A DATE
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
DECIDE `the application date` `is within twelve months after` `the incident date` IF
    BRANCH
       IF DATE_YEAR `the application date` LESS THAN    (DATE_YEAR `the incident date` PLUS 1) THEN TRUE
       IF DATE_YEAR `the application date` GREATER THAN (DATE_YEAR `the incident date` PLUS 1) THEN FALSE
       IF DATE_MONTH `the application date` LESS THAN    DATE_MONTH `the incident date` THEN TRUE
       IF DATE_MONTH `the application date` GREATER THAN DATE_MONTH `the incident date` THEN FALSE
       OTHERWISE DATE_DAY `the application date` AT MOST DATE_DAY `the incident date`

IMPORT `rbo-domain`

-- Retail Barring Orders Bill 2025 (WA) -- Part 1 s 6, and Part 2.
-- What retail violence is, who may apply, when a court may make an RBO, and
-- how long it lasts.
--
-- No library imports: see the note at the head of rbo-domain.l4 and incidents
-- H-03 and H-04 in INCIDENTS.md.

§ `Part 1 -- Preliminary`

§§ `6 -- Retail violence`

-- s 6(1): "A person commits retail violence if the person, while on retail
-- premises, engages in any of the following behaviour in relation to another
-- person on the retail premises".
--
-- The five paragraphs are the disjunction. The last rung spells OR rather than
-- taking the `..` sugar: a chain that ends in sugar never says what kind of
-- chain it is, and a chain that ends in sugar because someone deleted the final
-- rung looks exactly the same.
GIVEN incident IS AN Incident
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
DECIDE `the behaviour is of a kind listed in section 6(1)` IF
        "(a)" ... incident's `behaviour`'s `physical violence or abuse`
    ..  "(b)" ... incident's `behaviour`'s `sexual violence or abuse`
    ..  "(c)" ... incident's `behaviour`'s `threatening behaviour`
    ..  "(d)" ... incident's `behaviour`'s `stalking`
    OR  "(e)" ... incident's `behaviour`'s `harassing, intimidating or offensive behaviour`

-- Three conjuncts, in the order the subsection puts them: the actor is on the
-- premises; another person is on the premises; the behaviour answers to one of
-- the five paragraphs.
GIVEN incident IS AN Incident
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
DECIDE `the incident is retail violence under section 6(1)` IF
        "while on retail premises" ... incident's `the actor is on the premises`
    ... "in relation to another person on the retail premises" ... incident's `another person is on the premises`
    AND `the behaviour is of a kind listed in section 6(1)` incident

-- s 6(2): "A person who procures another person to commit retail violence is
-- taken to have also committed the retail violence."
--
-- A deeming provision, so it sits BESIDE s 6(1) as an alternative route to the
-- same conclusion, not inside it. Note what it does to the procurer's own
-- presence: s 6(1) requires the actor to be on the premises, and s 6(2) deems
-- the procurer to have committed the violence without requiring the procurer to
-- have been anywhere at all. That is what the subsection says, and it is
-- encoded as written.
GIVEN incident IS AN Incident
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
DECIDE `the actor commits retail violence` IF
        "(1)" ... `the incident is retail violence under section 6(1)` incident
    OR  "(2) ... is taken to have also committed the retail violence" ... incident's `the actor procured another to commit it`

§ `Part 2 -- Retail barring orders`

§§ `Division 1 -- Applying for an RBO`

§§§ `8 -- Who may apply for RBO`

-- s 8(3): each of four classes is an `eligible person` for retail premises.
-- Paragraph (b) is conditional on (a) failing -- "if there is no employer for
-- the retail premises" -- and (c) on the premises being in a shopping centre.
-- So the capacities are alternatives with their own conditions, which is a
-- CONSIDER over the capacity claimed, not a flat disjunction.
DECLARE ApplicantCapacity IS ONE OF
    `the employer for the retail premises`
    `the person who conducts the retail business`
    `the owner of the retail shopping centre or their authorised manager`
    `a union entitled to represent the retail workers`
    `none of the above`

DECLARE RBOApplication HAS
    `applicant capacity`                            IS AN ApplicantCapacity
    `there is an employer for the retail premises`  IS A BOOLEAN
    `incident`                                      IS AN Incident
    `premises stated in the application`            IS A Premises
    `date the application is made`                  IS A DATE
    `respondent`                                    IS A Person

GIVEN application IS AN RBOApplication
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
DECIDE `the applicant is an eligible person for the retail premises` IF
    CONSIDER application's `applicant capacity`
    WHEN `the employer for the retail premises` THEN TRUE
    WHEN `the person who conducts the retail business`
        THEN NOT application's `there is an employer for the retail premises`
    WHEN `the owner of the retail shopping centre or their authorised manager`
        THEN application's `premises stated in the application`'s `part of a retail shopping centre`
    WHEN `a union entitled to represent the retail workers` THEN TRUE
    OTHERWISE FALSE

-- s 8(2): "An RBO application cannot be made later than 12 months after the day
-- on which the retail violence is alleged to have been committed."
--
-- The window endpoint is built by ADDING a year to the earlier date, never by
-- subtracting from the later one. Incrementing the YEAR is the clamp-immune
-- direction and it is leap-safe, because the calendar does the work.
GIVEN application IS AN RBOApplication
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
DECIDE `the application is made within the section 8(2) period` IF
    (application's `date the application is made`) `is within twelve months after` (application's `incident`'s `date`)

§§ `Division 2 -- Making an RBO`

§§§ `11 -- Grounds for making RBO`

-- s 11(b): the person is likely to (i) commit retail violence on those premises
-- again; or (ii) otherwise stalk or harass a retail worker on those premises.
-- Both limbs are predictions and neither is computable from the incident, so
-- they are facts the court supplies. The court's satisfaction is a record
-- rather than a flag, so the encoding says WHO was satisfied of WHAT.
DECLARE CourtSatisfaction HAS
    `likely to commit retail violence on those premises again`  IS A BOOLEAN
    `likely to otherwise stalk or harass a retail worker there` IS A BOOLEAN
    `making the RBO is appropriate in the circumstances`        IS A BOOLEAN
    `the terms are the least restrictive possible`              IS A BOOLEAN

-- Identity is a field you compare, never the whole record.
GIVEN application IS AN RBOApplication
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
DECIDE `the incident was on the premises stated in the application` IF
         application's `incident`'s `premises`'s `name`
    EQUALS application's `premises stated in the application`'s `name`

GIVEN satisfaction IS A CourtSatisfaction
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
DECIDE `the person is likely to offend again on those premises` IF
        "(i)" ... satisfaction's `likely to commit retail violence on those premises again`
    OR  "(ii)" ... satisfaction's `likely to otherwise stalk or harass a retail worker there`

GIVEN application  IS AN RBOApplication
      satisfaction IS A CourtSatisfaction
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
DECIDE `grounds for making an RBO exist` IF
        "(a) the person has committed retail violence on the retail premises stated in the RBO application"
    ... `the actor commits retail violence` (application's `incident`)
    ... `the incident was on the premises stated in the application` application
    ... "(b) the person is likely to --" ... `the person is likely to offend again on those premises` satisfaction
    AND "(c) making the RBO is appropriate in the circumstances" ... satisfaction's `making the RBO is appropriate in the circumstances`

§§§ `10 -- Making RBO`

-- s 10: "A court may make an RBO against a person if -- (a) the court is
-- satisfied that -- (i) there are grounds ...; and (ii) the terms ... are the
-- least restrictive ...; and (b) the person is an individual who has reached 10
-- years of age."
--
-- The age floor in (b) is TEN, which is neither of the Bill's two defined age
-- classes -- `adult` (18 and over) and `child` (under 18). It appears once, so
-- it is carried as a fact about the respondent rather than as a third member of
-- `Age`: folding it in would make every age-sensitive rule in the Bill branch
-- three ways when all of them branch two ways.
GIVEN application IS AN RBOApplication
      satisfaction IS A CourtSatisfaction
      `the respondent has reached 10 years of age` IS A BOOLEAN
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
DECIDE `the court may make an RBO` IF
        "(a)(i) there are grounds for making the RBO under section 11" ... `grounds for making an RBO exist` application satisfaction
    ... "(a)(ii) the terms of the RBO are the least restrictive" ... satisfaction's `the terms are the least restrictive possible`
    AND "(b) the person is an individual who has reached 10 years of age" ... `the respondent has reached 10 years of age`

§§ `Division 3 -- When an RBO is in force`

§§§ `21 -- Duration of RBO`

-- s 21(2): a period the court specifies must be not longer than 2 years for an
-- adult, 1 year for a child.
GIVEN `age when made` IS AN Age
GIVETH A NUMBER
DECIDE `the maximum period in days` IS
    CONSIDER `age when made`
    WHEN `an adult` THEN 730
    WHEN `a child`  THEN 365

-- s 21(3): "Unless varied or cancelled under Part 3, an RBO remains in force
-- for -- (a) if a period is specified in the RBO -- that period ...; or (b) if
-- no period is specified ... and the person ... is an adult ... 2 years ...; or
-- (c) if no period is specified ... and the person ... is a child ... 1 year".
--
-- The MAYBE is matched, not folded: the absence of a specified period is a fact
-- about the order for which the statute then supplies a default, which is a
-- default the law provides rather than an outcome the law names.
GIVEN order IS AN RBO
GIVETH A NUMBER
DECIDE `the period for which the RBO remains in force, in days` IS
    CONSIDER order's `period specified in days`
    WHEN JUST period THEN period
    WHEN NOTHING     THEN `the maximum period in days` (order's `age when the RBO was made`)

-- s 21(2) constrains the COURT, so it is a predicate about the order rather
-- than part of the duration calculation: an order specifying longer than the
-- maximum is one the court had no power to make, not one that runs longer.
GIVEN order IS AN RBO
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
DECIDE `the specified period is within the section 21(2) limit` IF
    CONSIDER order's `period specified in days`
    WHEN NOTHING     THEN TRUE
    WHEN JUST period THEN
        period AT MOST `the maximum period in days` (order's `age when the RBO was made`)

IMPORT `rbo-domain`

-- Retail Barring Orders Bill 2025 (WA) -- Part 3, varying or cancelling an RBO.
--
-- This module is where incident B-01 lives. Section 39 enumerates the orders a
-- court may make, and enumerates a DIFFERENT set depending on which section
-- fixed the hearing. Encoding the two enumerations separately, as the section
-- writes them, is what makes the difference between them assertable.

§ `Part 3 -- Varying or cancelling an RBO`

§§ `Membership`

-- No prelude on this machine (H-04), so `elem` is unavailable and membership is
-- written out. Structural recursion over the list, which is all `elem` is.
GIVEN `the order`       IS AN AvailableOrder
      `the orders`      IS A LIST OF AvailableOrder
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
DECIDE `the order` `is among` `the orders` IF
    CONSIDER `the orders`
    WHEN EMPTY THEN FALSE
    WHEN head FOLLOWED BY tail THEN head EQUALS `the order` OR (`the order` `is among` tail)

§§ `39 -- Varying or cancelling RBO`

-- s 39(1): "At a hearing fixed under section 37 the court may make an order --
--   (a) dismissing the application to vary or cancel the RBO; or
--   (b) subject to subsection (4), varying the RBO; or
--   (c) cancelling the RBO."
--
-- s 39(2): "At a hearing fixed under section 38(1)(a) the court may make an
--   order cancelling the RBO."
--
-- Two subsections, two lists, and the whole of B-01 is the difference between
-- them. Section 39 says nothing at all about a hearing fixed under s 36, whose
-- outcomes (grant leave / dismiss) are s 36(2)'s own, so that arm is EMPTY --
-- an honest silence about section 39, not a claim that the court can do nothing.
GIVEN `the hearing` IS A HearingFixedUnder
GIVETH A LIST OF AvailableOrder
DECIDE `the orders the court may make under section 39` IS
    CONSIDER `the hearing`
    WHEN `section 37 -- an inter partes hearing` THEN
        LIST `dismissing the application to vary or cancel the RBO`,
             `varying the RBO`,
             `cancelling the RBO`
    WHEN `section 38(1)(a) -- a cancellation heard in the absence of the person bound` THEN
        LIST `cancelling the RBO`
    WHEN `section 36(1)(a) -- a leave hearing` THEN EMPTY

-- The operative question B-01 asks. A court that declines to grant an
-- application needs some order by which the application stops being on foot.
-- At a s 37 hearing that is s 39(1)(a). At a s 38(1)(a) hearing there is none.
GIVEN `the hearing` IS A HearingFixedUnder
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
DECIDE `the court may dismiss the application at this hearing` IF
    `dismissing the application to vary or cancel the RBO` `is among` (`the orders the court may make under section 39` `the hearing`)

§§ `The gap, named so that it can be asserted`

-- NOT THE BILL'S WORDS. `no order is available under section 39` corresponds to
-- no text in the Bill; it is the encoder's name for the state the Bill leaves
-- undescribed, and it exists so that B-01 can be demonstrated by an assertion
-- rather than argued in prose.
--
-- It is deliberately NOT a REFUSE. A refusal says the MODEL declines to answer.
-- Here the model is complete and the statute is not: every fact needed to
-- decide the case is present, and s 39 simply provides no order to make. Those
-- are different claims and only the second one is true.
DECLARE Section39Outcome IS ONE OF
    `the RBO is cancelled`
    `the application is dismissed`
    `no order is available under section 39`

GIVEN `the hearing` IS A HearingFixedUnder
      `the court is satisfied the RBO should be cancelled` IS A BOOLEAN
GIVETH A Section39Outcome
DECIDE `the outcome under section 39` IS
    IF   `the court is satisfied the RBO should be cancelled`
    THEN `the RBO is cancelled`
    ELSE IF `the court may dismiss the application at this hearing` `the hearing`
         THEN `the application is dismissed`
         ELSE `no order is available under section 39`

IMPORT `rbo-domain`

-- Retail Barring Orders Bill 2025 (WA) -- Part 5 Divisions 2 and 3.
-- How a relevant order is served, and what follows when the order is a
-- firearms RBO.
--
-- This module is where incident B-02 lives. Section 63's notification chain has
-- three links, and every link after the first is conditioned on the first. The
-- point of encoding service routes as a type is that the condition on the first
-- link can then be evaluated against every route the Bill allows, instead of
-- against the one route the drafter had in mind.

§ `Part 5 -- General`

§§ `Division 2 -- Service of summons for hearing or relevant order`

§§§ `54, 55, 57 -- When a relevant order is served`

-- s 54(1): a relevant order must be served by personal service unless
-- substituted service is allowed under s 56 or 57.
-- s 54(2): if the person bound is present in court when the order is made, the
-- order is TAKEN to have been served personally on them when it is made.
-- s 55(2): personal service must be effected by one of five classes of person.
-- s 57(5): where a senior police officer approves substituted service, the
-- order is served if the server takes the prescribed steps.
--
-- Every member of ServiceRoute is good service. That is the premise B-02 needs
-- and it is worth stating as its own rule rather than assuming it: the finding
-- is that the Bill treats these routes as equivalent for SERVICE and as wholly
-- different for the FIREARMS INQUIRY, and the first half has to be on the
-- record for the second half to be a finding.
GIVEN `the route` IS A ServiceRoute
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
DECIDE `the relevant order is served` IF
    CONSIDER `the route`
    WHEN `personal service by a registrar of the court`             THEN TRUE
    WHEN `personal service by a person authorised by a registrar`   THEN TRUE
    WHEN `personal service by a police officer`                     THEN TRUE
    WHEN `personal service by a custodial officer`                  THEN TRUE
    WHEN `personal service by a prison officer`                     THEN TRUE
    WHEN `service taken to have been effected by presence in court` THEN TRUE
    WHEN `substituted service effected orally by a police officer`  THEN TRUE
    WHEN `substituted service effected by post`                     THEN TRUE
    WHEN `substituted service effected by electronic means`         THEN TRUE

§§ `Division 3 -- Other matters`

§§§ `63 -- Notification of firearms RBO`

-- The facts s 63 turns on beyond the order and the route.
DECLARE FirearmsCircumstances HAS
    `the restrained person uses a firearm item in their usual occupation` IS A BOOLEAN
    `a co-licensee holds an authorisation for the same firearm item`      IS A BOOLEAN

-- s 63(2): "A police officer who serves a firearms RBO personally or effects
-- substituted service of a firearms RBO under section 56(3) or 57(5) ORALLY
-- must -- (a) ask the restrained person [the four questions]; and (b) complete
-- the relevant part of the POLICE COPY of the firearms RBO ...".
--
-- Two limbs, and both of them are narrow. The first requires the server to be a
-- police officer; the second requires the substituted service to have been
-- effected orally. Six of the nine routes in `ServiceRoute` satisfy neither.
GIVEN `the route` IS A ServiceRoute
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
DECIDE `section 63(2) obliges the server to ask the firearms questions` IF
        "a police officer who serves a firearms RBO personally" ... `the route` EQUALS `personal service by a police officer`
    OR  "or effects substituted service ... orally" ... `the route` EQUALS `substituted service effected orally by a police officer`

-- The first link. There is no police copy unless a police officer completed one
-- under s 63(2)(b).
GIVEN `the order` IS AN RBO
      `the route` IS A ServiceRoute
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
DECIDE `a completed police copy of the firearms RBO exists` IF
        `the order`'s `prohibits possession of a firearm item`
    AND `section 63(2) obliges the server to ask the firearms questions` `the route`

-- s 63(4): "ON RECEIPT OF THE POLICE COPY of a firearms RBO that indicates that
-- the restrained person uses or has access to a firearm item in the course of
-- the person's usual occupation, or holds a firearms authorisation in respect
-- of a firearm item for which a co-licensee also holds a firearms
-- authorisation, the Commissioner of Police must promptly notify the
-- responsible person or co-licensee ...".
--
-- The second link, and the conditional opening clause is the hinge of B-02.
GIVEN `the order`         IS AN RBO
      `the route`         IS A ServiceRoute
      `the circumstances` IS A FirearmsCircumstances
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
DECIDE `the Commissioner must notify under section 63(4)` IF
        "On receipt of the police copy of a firearms RBO" ... `a completed police copy of the firearms RBO exists` `the order` `the route`
    AND `the circumstances is one section 63(4) covers` `the circumstances`

GIVEN `the circumstances` IS A FirearmsCircumstances
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
DECIDE `the circumstances is one section 63(4) covers` IF
        "uses or has access to a firearm item in the course of the person's usual occupation" ... `the circumstances`'s `the restrained person uses a firearm item in their usual occupation`
    OR  "or holds a firearms authorisation ... for which a co-licensee also holds" ... `the circumstances`'s `a co-licensee holds an authorisation for the same firearm item`

-- s 63(5): "A RESPONSIBLE PERSON NOTIFIED UNDER SUBSECTION (4) who allows the
-- restrained person to use or have access to a firearm item commits an
-- offence."  s 63(6) is the same shape for a co-licensee.
--
-- The third link. Both offences are drafted as offences by a person "notified
-- under subsection (4)", so an unnotified responsible person or co-licensee
-- cannot commit them however dangerous their conduct. That is the consequence
-- B-02 records: the gap in s 63(2) does not merely delay paperwork, it
-- disapplies two offence provisions.
GIVEN `the order`         IS AN RBO
      `the route`         IS A ServiceRoute
      `the circumstances` IS A FirearmsCircumstances
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
DECIDE `a responsible person could commit the section 63(5) offence` IF
    `the Commissioner must notify under section 63(4)` `the order` `the route` `the circumstances`
